transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I know people at my apartment are watching when I come and go. They’ve been slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody tells me they’re just regular notices on the doors, but I don’t think that’s all it is.

Besides these suspicions about your neighbors, have you noticed any recent changes in your mood, like feeling unusually elated, irritable, or full of energy, or on the other hand feeling very sad, hopeless, or low?
Most mornings I wake up feeling really heavy and hollow, like the day’s already gone bad before I even get out of bed.
How long have you been feeling that your neighbors are watching and reporting on you?
It’s been about a year and a month now.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hollow low mood - has it been going on for the whole year that you've felt watched, or did it start more recently?
It’s been going on about a year and two months, I think. The heavy, no-point feeling, and I’ve been pulling away from things for that long.
Have there been times when your mood felt normal or better, but you still believed your neighbors were watching and reporting on you?
Yeah. There was a stretch of a few weeks where I was eating a little better and not waking up quite so hopeless. But I still believed the neighbors were watching my door and reporting on me.

Looking back over the whole 14 months, would you say you've been feeling this heavy, hopeless way most of the time, or has it actually been more the exception, with longer stretches where your mood was okay even though you still believed you were being watched?
Most of the time, yeah. Even on days when I seemed a little clearer, I still felt low and useless, and I wasn't interested in the things I used to do.
Did you start believing your neighbors were watching and reporting on you before you started feeling this heavy, hopeless mood, or did both begin around the same time?
They kind of go together. When I’m down in that hollow place—barely eating or answering the phone—that’s when I’m most sure the apartment people are tracking me and talking to the office about me.

During that few-week stretch when your mood was a bit better, were you completely free of any low mood, low energy, or loss of interest, or did some of those depressive feelings still linger even though they were milder?
No, it wasn’t completely gone. Most mornings I’d still wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day had already gone bad before I even got out of bed.
Before this past year and two months, had you ever gone through a similar period of feeling this heavy, hopeless, and withdrawn that later fully lifted, at some earlier point in your life?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a time before this where I felt that way and then it fully went away.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a 14-month episode of persistent depressed mood ('heavy, hollow' feeling), anhedonia, low energy, poor appetite, and social withdrawal occurring most of the time, meeting duration and severity criteria for a major depressive episode. Concurrently, she holds a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (neighbors surveilling and reporting on her) that intensifies during depressive lows and remains present, though somewhat attenuated, during brief periods of symptomatic improvement. The delusion emerged in close temporal association with the depressive episode and has no clear existence independent of it, and there is no history of a prior manic/hypomanic episode or a psychotic disorder predating the mood disturbance. This pattern is most consistent with a single episode of severe major depressive disorder with psychotic features (mood-congruent/incongruent persecutory delusions) rather than schizoaffective disorder or a primary psychotic disorder, since the psychotic symptoms have not been sustained during a sufficiently long period of euthymia.
